'''Ingo Burgert''' (born 1968) is a German-Swiss [[Wood science|wood scientist]] and professor at the [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]], Institute for Building Materials,<ref name="ETHbio">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Ingo Burgert |department=Institute for Building Materials |website=ETH Zürich |url=https://ifb.ethz.ch/the-institute/people/person-detail.MTgyMjI2.TGlzdC8xMDYwLC0xNTk5MjE4NDY3.html |access-date=2025-07-18 |archive-date=2025-03-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250321235408/https://ifb.ethz.ch/the-institute/people/person-detail.MTgyMjI2.TGlzdC8xMDYwLC0xNTk5MjE4NDY3.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607030054/https://www.iaws-web.org/organisation/executive-committee/ |url-status=live }}</ref> who is a ''[[Fellow]]'' of the [[International Academy of Wood Science]] (IAWS).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2270527-wooden-floors-rotted-by-fungi-generate-electricity-when-walked-on/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250615102603/https://www.newscientist.com/article/2270527-wooden-floors-rotted-by-fungi-generate-electricity-when-walked-on/ |archive-date=2025-06-15 ==Career==
Burgert studied wood science and technology at the [[University of Hamburg]], earning a diploma in 1995 and a doctorate degree in wood biology in 2000. 

He conducted postdoctoral research at BOKU Vienna (2000–2003), then led the Plant Biomechanics & Biomimetics group at the Max Planck Institute, Potsdam (2003–2011). In 2011, he became a full professor at ETH Zürich and co-leads the WoodTec group at Empa.<ref name="ETHbio"/>

Burgert’s research addresses wood’s structure from nano- to macro- scale, enabling polymer and nanobased modifications to enhance durability, stability, and functionality. His group has developed electrically conductive "wood electronics" via laser induced graphitization, suitable for smart building sensors, and explores reversible wood–water actuation and piezoelectric composites.<ref name="ETHbio"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dreimol |first1=Christopher H. |last2=Guo |first2=Huizhang |last3=Ritter |first3=Maximilian |last4=Keplinger |first4=Tobias |last5=Ding |first5=Yong |last6=Günther |first6=Roman |last7=Poloni |first7=Erik |last8=Burgert |first8=Ingo |last9=Panzarasa |first9=Guido |title=Sustainable wood electronics by iron-catalyzed laser-induced graphitization for large-scale applications |journal=Nature Communications |date=2022 |volume=13 |article-number=3680 |doi=10.1038/s41467-022-31283-7  |doi-access=free|pmid=35760793 |bibcode=2022NatCo..13.3680D |pmc=9237073 }}</ref> 

In 2018, his novel work earned the Heinzel Mondi Sappi Award for "Delignified and Densified Cellulose Bulk Materials" by the ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces,<ref name="ETHbio"/> and he received the 2020 SDG Award for his research work towards the sustainability.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.empa.ch/web/s604/nachhaltigkeitsaward_sdg |title=Wood as high-performance material |date=3 September 2020 |first=Andrea |last=Six |website=[[Empa]]}}</ref>

In October 2023, a [[metascience|meta-research]] carried out by [[John Ioannidis]] et al. at [[Stanford University]] included Burgert in Elsevier Data 2022, where he was ranked at the top 2% of researchers in wood science globally ("forestry – nanoscience/nanotechnology").<ref>{{cite book | last=Baas | first=Jeroen | title=October 2023 data-update for 'Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators' | chapter=Bibliometrics | date=2023 | volume=6 | publisher=Elsevier Data Repository | doi=10.17632/BTCHXKTZYW.6 | chapter-url=https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btchxktzyw/6 | access-date=2025-07-18 | archive-date=2024-02-27 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240227060821/https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btchxktzyw/6 | url-status=live }}</ref> In August 2024, Ingo Burgert has been also included for his research work in [[wood science]] at the [[Science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators|Stanford/Elsevier top 2% list]], having a high [[Composite index (metrics)|c-score]] of 3.6912.<ref>{{cite book | last=Ioannidis | first=John P.A. | title=August 2024 data-update for 'Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators' | chapter=Bibliometrics | date=2024 | volume=7 | publisher=Elsevier Data Repository | doi=10.17632/BTCHXKTZYW.7 | chapter-url=https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btchxktzyw/7 | access-date=2025-07-18 | page=line: 52,085}} (career data)</ref> He also received the same distinction in 2025.

In January 2026, he and his fellow researcher Eleni Chatzi, received from ETH the Dandelion Entrepreneurship Awards for their applied research work.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mickein |first=Iris |title=ETH Entrepreneurship Award for Eleni Chatzi and Ingo Burgert |website=Dept. of Civil |date=2026-02-23 |url=https://baug.ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/news/2026/01/eth-entrepreneurship-award-for-eleni-chatzi-and-ingo-burgert.html |access-date=2026-08-26}}</ref>

Until August 2026, the research work of Burgert has received more than '''20,000''' citations at [[Google Scholar]], having a high [[h-index]] of 77.<ref>{{cite web | title=Ingo Burgert | website=Google Scholar | url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=0_q-ekYAAAAJ | access-date=2026-08-26}}</ref>
